solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Dreadful boob amidst clues is confusing!

indicators.note: dreadful work is badly done, a sign that the letters of the words beside it are jumbled

explanation.surface: A setter's awful blunder buried among the clues leaves the solver baffled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'amidst' looks like a link placing the boob among the clues, but it is part of the fodder: BOOB, AMIDST and CLUES together supply all fifteen letters, rearranged as 'Dreadful' signals.
explanation.definitionFit: To discombobulate is a jocular verb meaning to bewilder or throw into disorder, so the answer is a synonym of is confusing.

clue.text: Cop outdistances criminal finding sources of funds

indicators.note: something criminal is crooked or bent, a sign that the letters of the words before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A villain outrunning the police turns out to be the way the money is traced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' looks like a noun for the person being chased, but it is the anagram signal applied to COP and OUTDISTANCES together.
explanation.definitionFit: Bank accounts holding savings on deposit are places money is drawn from, hence sources of funds.

clue.text: More confident about company, one cleans up

indicators.note: about means the word for more confident goes round the abbreviation for company

parts.note: more confident, more certain, is surer

explanation.surface: A firm's boss, increasingly self-assured, turns out to be the office cleaner.
explanation.definitionFit: A scourer is a pad or person that scrubs pans clean, so it is something that cleans up.

clue.text: Charge too much for crop initially — I reprove angrily

indicators.note: angrily suggests agitation, so the letters before it are thrown into a new order
initially points to just the opening letter of the word crop

explanation.surface: A farmer is scolded for asking an outrageous price for the harvest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes C from 'crop'; 'angrily' rearranges C with I and REPROVE.
explanation.definitionFit: To overprice is to set a cost higher than something is worth, which is to charge too much for it.

clue.text: Poet feels strong emotion

definitions.meaning: Robert ..., the national poet of Scotland
one who ... with anger or passion is consumed by a strong feeling

explanation.surface: A poet is moved by passionate feelings.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Burns is the famous Scottish poet, and to burn is to be inflamed with anger or desire.

clue.text: Wood workers, ones celebrating wildly when rector becomes bishop

indicators.note: becomes says one letter turns into another inside the word for the partygoers

parts.note: revellers are people having a riotous party
B is the chess notation abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: Carpenters party hard after a clergyman is promoted to bishop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when rector becomes bishop' tells you to change the R of REVELLERS into B.
explanation.definitionFit: Bevellers cut sloping edges on timber, so they are craftsmen who work wood.

clue.text: Generous contribution from popular German

indicators.note: contribution from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A well-liked German gives a lavish donation.
explanation.definitionFit: Large can mean liberal or bountiful, as in a large-hearted gesture, so it is a synonym for generous.

clue.text: Craft if moving?

indicators.note: moving says the letters of the two words before it are shifted about

explanation.surface: Boats and planes in motion make up the flow along a route.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: rearrange CRAFT IF, and the result is what vessels in motion are.
explanation.definitionFit: Traffic is the vehicles, ships or aircraft travelling along a route, so it is craft that are moving.

clue.text: Value highly having firm, Harrods, say, alongside

parts.note: firm, as in a set jelly, means set
Harrods, the famous London department store, is an example of a great store
by means beside or alongside

explanation.surface: Shoppers prize a solid department store such as Harrods.
explanation.walkthrough: Harrods is a large luxury department store in Knightsbridge, London; 'say' flags it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: To set great store by something is an idiom meaning to regard it as very important.

clue.text: Original developer of waterside feature one secured

indicators.note: secured means the structure holds the other word fast inside it

parts.note: a pier is a structure jutting out from the shore
taken as written

explanation.surface: The first builder of a seaside jetty made one fast.
explanation.definitionFit: A pioneer is the first to explore or develop something, so an original developer.

clue.text: It's unusual and courageous to change sides

indicators.note: change sides tells you to swap left for right, the letter for one side becoming that for the other

parts.note: courageous means valiant

explanation.surface: Defecting is described as rare yet brave.
explanation.walkthrough: Sides are left and right, L and R: VALIANT with its L turned to R.
explanation.definitionFit: A variant is a form differing from the usual one, so something out of the ordinary.

clue.text: Charge after second college fight

indicators.note: after places the word for charge behind the two abbreviations

parts.note: a rap is a criminal charge, as in a murder rap

explanation.surface: A second student is accused after a brawl on campus.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrap is informal for a scuffle or brawl, a synonym of fight.

clue.text: Tree gets second prize, sixty per cent of first

parts.note: silver is the medal for second place

indicators.note: sixty per cent of a five-letter word is its opening three letters

explanation.surface: A tree is placed second, with three-fifths of the winner's score.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sixty per cent of' takes three of the five letters of 'first', FIR.
explanation.definitionFit: The silver fir is a European conifer, a kind of tree.

clue.text: Conclude irate men ultimately must reform

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word must
reform means form again, so the letters are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: Angry men must eventually change their ways to bring things to a close.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' gives T, the last of 'must'; 'reform' rearranges T with IRATE MEN.
explanation.definitionFit: To terminate is to bring to an end, so a synonym of conclude.

clue.text: Excited parent at opening of modern place to live

indicators.note: excited means stirred up, a sign the letters are mixed
opening of points to the first letter of the word modern

explanation.surface: A thrilled father or mother moves into a newly built home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opening of' gives M from 'modern'; 'Excited' rearranges it with PARENT AT.
explanation.definitionFit: An apartment is a flat, a set of rooms used as a home.

clue.text: Drink, jar of choice, regularly brought over

indicators.note: brought over means turned back, so the picked letters are read in the other direction
regularly picks every other letter of the phrase

explanation.surface: A favourite cup of something is fetched over.
explanation.walkthrough: Every second letter of 'jar of choice' gives A O C O C; 'brought over' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Cocoa is a hot chocolate beverage, a kind of drink.

clue.text: Fuss after removing covers, scary agent cut diamond

indicators.note: after places the word for fuss below the others in this down entry
removing covers strips off the outer letters of the word scary
cut means trimmed, so the last letter comes off

parts.note: Bond, James Bond, is the fictional secret agent
ado means fuss or bother

explanation.surface: A frightening spy creates a stir after unmasking, then cuts a gem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removing covers' takes CAR from sCARy; 'cut' docks BOND to BON.
explanation.definitionFit: Carbonado is a dark, opaque form of diamond used in industry, also called black diamond.

clue.text: Country kid changed in the end

indicators.note: changed in the end says the final letter of the word for kid is swapped for another

parts.note: a kid is a child

explanation.surface: A youngster eventually switches nationality.
explanation.walkthrough: CHILD's last letter, D, becomes E.
explanation.definitionFit: Chile is a South American nation along the Pacific coast.

clue.text: No native icon relaxing overlooking French waters

indicators.note: in a down entry overlooking puts one part above the other
relaxing means loosening up, so the letters of icon are rearranged

parts.note: mer is the French word for sea

explanation.surface: An outsider, not a native celebrity, lounges with a view of the French sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relaxing' rearranges ICON to INCO, and 'overlooking' places it above MER.
explanation.definitionFit: An incomer is a newcomer who has moved into an area, so is not a native of it.

clue.text: Sinatra broadcast associated with US nationals

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are strewn into a new order

explanation.surface: A Frank Sinatra radio show is linked with America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' rearranges SINATRA together with US; 'associated with' joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: Austrians are citizens of Austria, nationals of that country.

clue.text: Gets to answer, that's terrific, announces inexperienced novice solver just starting

indicators.note: just starting picks the opening letter of each of the words before it

parts.words: that's terrific, announces inexperienced novice solver

explanation.surface: A beginner announces a triumphant answer when getting a clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'just starting' takes the first letters of 'that's terrific announces inexperienced novice solver', TTAINS.
explanation.definitionFit: To attain is to reach or achieve, so a synonym of gets to.

clue.text: Players upset her co-star

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: An actor's fellow star is distressed.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchestra is a group of musicians, who are players of instruments.

clue.text: Guy from north in lake

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for north inside the name of the lake

parts.note: Erie is one of the North American Great Lakes

explanation.surface: A man from the north is in a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernie is a man's name, and guy means a man.

clue.text: Lively following drink? Right!

parts.note: ale is beer, a drink

explanation.surface: Feeling sprightly after a drink? Quite!
explanation.definitionFit: Alert means wide awake and quick to respond, hence lively.

clue.text: Old, retired workers joining party — that's better!

indicators.note: retired means withdrawn or gone back, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: TU is a trade union, an organisation of workers
a do is a party

explanation.surface: Pensioners joining a celebration claim it is an improvement.
explanation.definitionFit: To outdo is to surpass, so a verb meaning to better.

clue.text: Candidate — minor figure: note indication of name change

parts.note: NO is the abbreviation for number, a figure
mi is the third note of the sol-fa scale
nee, meaning born, marks a woman's former surname after marriage

explanation.surface: A candidate is a minor player, as a note on a name change shows.
explanation.walkthrough: Née is a French word placed before a married woman's maiden name.
explanation.definitionFit: A nominee is someone put forward for office or an award, a candidate.

clue.text: Investigate old American explosive device

parts.note: ex means former, so old
a mine is a buried bomb

explanation.surface: A former American looks into a bomb.
explanation.definitionFit: To examine is to inspect closely, a synonym of investigate.

clue.text: Roué, lusty spirit, working with stealth

indicators.note: working means in operation or being worked over, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: A lecherous rake with a randy temperament operates covertly.
explanation.definitionFit: Surreptitiously means secretly or furtively, acting with stealth.
